subchapter: 3.5-Advanced Importing of Keywords and Naming Conflicts

questions.question: What happens when a suite imports a resource file that itself imports other resource files and libraries?

options.text: The suite has access to all keywords, variables, and libraries from all transitively imported files
The suite only has access to keywords and variables defined directly in the imported resource file
options.explanation: Robot Framework supports transitive imports, making all nested imports available

options.text: The suite must explicitly import each library and resource file individually
options.explanation: Transitive imports automatically make nested resources available

options.text: Only variables are transitively imported, not keywords or libraries
options.explanation: All elements (keywords, variables, libraries) are transitively imported

questions.question: Which import pattern should be avoided in Robot Framework?

options.text: Circular imports where A.resource imports B.resource and B.resource imports A.resource
Importing multiple libraries in a single resource file
options.explanation: This is a common and acceptable practice for organizing imports

options.text: Importing resource files that contain only variables
options.explanation: Variable-only resource files are valid and useful for organization

options.text: Creating hierarchical import structures with multiple levels
options.explanation: Hierarchical imports are supported and useful for organization

questions.question: What happens when the same library with the exact same configuration is imported multiple times in different resource files?

options.text: Robot Framework ignores subsequent imports because it already has the library in its catalog
Robot Framework creates multiple instances of the library with separate keyword sets
options.explanation: Duplicate imports with identical configuration are ignored to avoid redundancy

options.text: Robot Framework throws an error about duplicate imports
options.explanation: No error is thrown; the duplicate import is simply ignored

options.text: The library is reloaded, clearing any state from previous imports
options.explanation: The library is not reloaded; the existing import is retained

questions.question: What is the recommended practice for importing libraries that are needed in multiple places?

options.text: Import the library only in one resource file with one configuration and use that resource file everywhere it's needed
Import the library directly in every suite that needs it to make dependencies explicit
options.explanation: This can lead to multiple imports and potential configuration conflicts

options.text: Import the library with different configurations in different files to customize behavior per context
options.explanation: Multiple configurations can cause side effects and unpredictable behavior

options.text: Avoid importing the same library in more than three resource files
options.explanation: The recommendation is to import only once, not multiple times with a limit

questions.question: Where is library configuration information documented?

options.text: In the library documentation's Importing section, directly before the list of keywords
In a separate configuration file with .libconf extension
options.explanation: Library configuration is documented in the library's own documentation

options.text: In the *** Settings *** section of the library source code
options.explanation: Library documentation contains the configuration details, not the source code settings

options.text: In the Robot Framework user guide under Library Configuration
options.explanation: Configuration is specific to each library and documented in that library's documentation

questions.question: How are library import arguments specified?

options.text: After the library name/path, separated by multiple spaces, similar to keyword arguments
In a separate [Arguments] setting within the *** Settings *** section
options.explanation: Library arguments follow the library name directly, not in a separate setting

options.text: Using the CONFIG keyword before importing the library
options.explanation: No CONFIG keyword exists; arguments follow the Library statement

options.text: In a dictionary variable passed to the Library statement
options.explanation: Arguments are passed directly as space-separated values, not as a dictionary

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Telnet    newline=LF    encoding=ISO-8859-1
```

What type of arguments are being used in this library import?

options.text: Named arguments
Positional arguments
options.explanation: The arguments use name=value format, which indicates named arguments

options.text: Embedded arguments
options.explanation: Embedded arguments are used in keyword names, not library imports

options.text: Configuration dictionary arguments
options.explanation: These are individual named arguments, not a dictionary structure

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use named arguments for library configuration?

options.text: Makes usage more readable
Makes usage more future-proof
Named arguments execute faster than positional arguments
options.explanation: There is no performance difference between named and positional arguments

options.text: Positional arguments are deprecated for library imports
options.explanation: Positional arguments are still valid, just not recommended

questions.question: What is a Remote library in Robot Framework?

options.text: A library running as a server that Robot Framework connects to as a client via network
A library that can be imported from a remote Git repository
options.explanation: Remote libraries refer to network-connected library servers, not source code repositories

options.text: A library that executes keywords on remote machines via SSH
options.explanation: SSHLibrary provides SSH functionality; Remote library is about network-based keyword servers

options.text: A third-party library not maintained by the Robot Framework Foundation
options.explanation: This describes external libraries; Remote is a specific built-in library type

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Remote    uri=http://127.0.0.1:8270    AS    EmbeddedAPI
Library    Remote    uri=http://remote.devices.local:8270    AS    DeviceAPI
```

Why is the AS statement necessary in this example?

options.text: To define unique library names since there are multiple Remote library instances with different configurations
AS is always required when using named arguments in library imports
options.explanation: AS is only needed when importing the same library multiple times with different configurations

options.text: To create aliases for easier typing of library names
options.explanation: While AS does create an alias, the primary purpose here is to distinguish multiple Remote library instances

options.text: Remote libraries require the AS statement for security reasons
options.explanation: AS is needed to distinguish multiple instances, not for security

questions.question: Given the import `Library    Remote    uri=http://127.0.0.1:8270    AS    EmbeddedAPI`, how would you call a keyword named `Close Contact` from this library?

options.text: EmbeddedAPI.Close Contact
Remote.Close Contact
options.explanation: When AS is used, the defined name (EmbeddedAPI) becomes the library prefix, not the original name (Remote)

options.text: Close Contact
options.explanation: While this might work if there are no conflicts, the question asks about proper usage with the AS name

options.text: http://127.0.0.1:8270.Close Contact
options.explanation: The URI is not used as a prefix; the AS name is used

questions.question: When do naming conflicts occur in Robot Framework?

options.text: When two or more keywords have the same name
When two libraries are imported with the same configuration
options.explanation: Identical imports are simply ignored; they don't cause conflicts

options.text: When a variable name matches a keyword name
options.explanation: Variables and keywords have different syntax and don't conflict with each other

options.text: When a resource file name matches a library name
options.explanation: File names don't cause naming conflicts; only keyword names do

questions.question: What tool can help detect naming conflicts when creating duplicate user keyword names?

options.text: A proper IDE that warns about duplicate user keyword names
The robot --check-duplicates command
options.explanation: No such command exists; IDEs provide this functionality

options.text: The libdoc tool when generating documentation
options.explanation: Libdoc generates documentation but doesn't check for naming conflicts across files

options.text: The rebot post-processing tool
options.explanation: Rebot processes output files; it doesn't check for naming conflicts

questions.question: Which two libraries are commonly known to have naming conflicts with each other?

options.text: Telnet and SSHLibrary
Collections and BuiltIn
options.explanation: These libraries are designed to work together without conflicts

options.text: SeleniumLibrary and Browser
options.explanation: While both handle web automation, they are typically not used together

options.text: String and OperatingSystem
options.explanation: These libraries have different purposes and few overlapping keyword names

questions.question: Why do Telnet and SSHLibrary have multiple keywords with the same names?

options.text: They both work with network connections and have similar functionality
SSHLibrary was designed as a drop-in replacement for Telnet
options.explanation: They are separate libraries with similar domains, not designed as replacements

options.text: They share a common base class that defines standard keyword names
options.explanation: The similar names arise from similar functionality, not inheritance

options.text: It's a design flaw that should be reported as a bug
options.explanation: It's an expected consequence of libraries with similar domains, handled by full naming

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Telnet
Library    SSHLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Example
    Open Connection    ${host}
```

What error message would Robot Framework give for this test?

options.text: Multiple keywords with name 'Open Connection' found. Give the full name of the keyword you want to use
Library conflict: Cannot import both Telnet and SSHLibrary in the same suite
options.explanation: Both libraries can be imported; the conflict is resolved at keyword call time

options.text: Ambiguous keyword call: Please specify which library to use
options.explanation: The actual error message is more specific and includes available options

options.text: Open Connection requires library prefix when multiple implementations exist
options.explanation: This captures the concept but not the actual error message format

questions.question: What is the easiest way to resolve naming conflicts from imported libraries?

options.text: Use the full name of the keyword, including the library name as a prefix
Import only one of the conflicting libraries per suite
options.explanation: This avoids the conflict but prevents using both libraries, which may be necessary

options.text: Create wrapper user keywords with unique names
options.explanation: While this works, it's more complex than using full keyword names

options.text: Use the WITH NAME statement to rename one library
options.explanation: The correct statement is AS, not WITH NAME

questions.question:
```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Using Telnet and SSHLibrary
    Telnet.Open Connection
    Telnet.Login    ${username}    ${password}
    ${telnet_init} =    Telnet.Read Until Prompt
    Telnet.Close Connection
    
    SSHLibrary.Open Connection    ${host}    ${port}
    SSHLibrary.Login    ${username}    ${password}
    ${ssh_init} =    SSHLibrary.Read Until Prompt
    SSHLibrary.Close Connection
```

What technique is being used to avoid naming conflicts?

options.text: Full keyword names with library prefix
Library aliasing with AS statements
options.explanation: While AS could be used, this example shows direct library prefixing without AS

options.text: Embedded arguments in keyword calls
options.explanation: This shows library prefixing, not embedded arguments

options.text: Named arguments for disambiguation
options.explanation: Named arguments don't resolve library conflicts; library prefixes do

questions.question: Can Robot Framework automatically resolve naming conflicts from the same type of source (e.g., two libraries)?

options.text: No, Robot Framework cannot resolve conflicts from the same source type and requires explicit full names
Yes, Robot Framework uses the most recently imported library
options.explanation: Robot Framework does not make assumptions; it requires explicit resolution

options.text: Yes, Robot Framework uses the library imported first
options.explanation: Import order doesn't resolve conflicts; explicit naming is required

options.text: Yes, Robot Framework prompts the user at runtime to choose
options.explanation: Robot Framework raises an error; it doesn't provide runtime prompts

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Remote    uri=http://api.server.local:8270    AS    API

*** Test Cases ***
Call Remote Keyword
    API.Initialize System
    API.Get Status    device_id=15
```

What would happen if you tried to call `Remote.Initialize System` instead of `API.Initialize System`?

options.text: Error: No keyword with name 'Remote.Initialize System' found
It would work the same as API.Initialize System
options.explanation: Once AS is used, only the new name is valid as a prefix

options.text: It would connect to the default Remote library location instead
options.explanation: There is no default location; the AS name replaces the original name

options.text: Robot Framework would warn but still execute the keyword
options.explanation: This would be an error, not a warning

questions.question:
Consider this structure:
```
A.resource imports: LibraryX, B.resource
B.resource imports: LibraryY, C.resource
C.resource imports: LibraryZ
suite.robot imports: A.resource
```

Which libraries are available to suite.robot?

options.text: LibraryX, LibraryY, and LibraryZ (all transitively imported libraries)
Only LibraryX (directly imported by A.resource)
options.explanation: Transitive imports make all nested libraries available

options.text: LibraryX and LibraryY (one level of transitive import)
options.explanation: All levels of transitive imports are available, not just one level

options.text: None, suite.robot must import libraries directly
options.explanation: Resource file imports are transitively available to importing suites

questions.question: What happens if a library is imported with different configurations in multiple resource files?

options.text: The library may be imported multiple times, potentially causing side effects or unpredictable behavior
Robot Framework merges the configurations and uses combined settings
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't merge configurations; each different configuration may create a new instance

options.text: Robot Framework raises an error about conflicting configurations
options.explanation: No error is raised; the behavior depends on the library's internal handling

options.text: The last imported configuration overrides all previous ones
options.explanation: The effect depends on the library; there's no guaranteed override behavior

questions.question: What is strongly recommended for library importing arguments according to the syllabus?

options.text: All arguments should be defined with default values in the library
All arguments should be passed as named arguments when importing
options.explanation: While recommended for usage, the syllabus states default values should be in the library itself

options.text: Arguments should be documented in a separate configuration file
options.explanation: Arguments should have default values in the library, not separate documentation

options.text: Libraries should avoid having any configuration arguments
options.explanation: Configuration is often necessary; the recommendation is about default values

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    common.resource
Library     DatabaseLibrary

# common.resource contains:
# Library    DatabaseLibrary
```

What happens with the DatabaseLibrary import?

options.text: The second import in the suite is ignored because it's already in the catalog with the same configuration
DatabaseLibrary is loaded twice, creating two independent instances
options.explanation: Identical imports are deduplicated by Robot Framework

options.text: Robot Framework raises a warning about duplicate imports
options.explanation: No warning is raised; duplicate imports are silently ignored

options.text: The import in the suite overrides the import from the resource file
options.explanation: There's no override; the first import is used and subsequent ones are ignored

questions.question: Which of these are examples of common keywords that conflict between Telnet and SSHLibrary?

options.text: Open Connection
Login
Read
Close Connection
Execute Command
options.explanation: While both might have similar keywords, Execute Command is not specifically mentioned in the syllabus

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    MyLibrary    timeout=30    retry=3
Library    MyLibrary    timeout=60    retry=5
```

According to best practices, what's wrong with this import pattern?

options.text: The same library is being imported with different configurations, which should be avoided
Library names must be unique, so the second import should use AS
options.explanation: While AS could help, the fundamental issue is importing with different configurations

options.text: Named arguments should not be used for numeric values
options.explanation: Named arguments work fine with numeric values; the issue is multiple imports

options.text: Libraries can only be imported once per *** Settings *** section
options.explanation: Multiple imports are technically possible; the issue is that it's not recommended

questions.question: What is the purpose of hierarchical organization of imports using resource files?

options.text: To organize user keywords and library imports in a structured way
To make keywords and variables transitively available through resource file imports
To improve test execution performance by caching imports
options.explanation: Organization is for maintainability, not performance optimization

options.text: To enforce access control and prevent unauthorized keyword usage
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't provide access control; all imports are available

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    Telnet    timeout=10s
Library    SSHLibrary

*** Test Cases ***
Test Connection
    Open Connection    ${host}
```

How should this be fixed to avoid the naming conflict?

options.text: Use Telnet.Open Connection or SSHLibrary.Open Connection
Add AS TelnetLib and AS SSHLib to the imports
options.explanation: While AS could work, using the direct library name as prefix is simpler and recommended

options.text: Remove the timeout argument from Telnet import
options.explanation: Configuration arguments don't affect naming conflicts

options.text: Import only one library per test case
options.explanation: Both libraries can be used; the conflict is resolved with full keyword names

questions.question: If a library cannot work without configuration arguments, what should be done?

options.text: Pass the required configuration arguments when importing the library
Create a wrapper resource file that sets default values
options.explanation: While possible, the direct approach is to pass arguments at import time

options.text: Configure the library using Set Library Search Order keyword
options.explanation: This keyword is for resolving conflicts, not for library configuration

options.text: Use environment variables to configure the library externally
options.explanation: While some libraries support this, the standard approach is import-time arguments

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    tech_keywords.resource

# tech_keywords.resource contains:
# Library    Collections
# Library    String
# Resource   variables.resource
#
# variables.resource contains:
# Library    OperatingSystem
```

Which libraries are available in the suite?

options.text: Collections, String, and OperatingSystem
Only Collections and String
options.explanation: OperatingSystem is also available through transitive import

options.text: None, the suite must import libraries directly
options.explanation: Libraries imported by resource files are available to the suite

options.text: Only OperatingSystem from the most deeply nested resource
options.explanation: All transitively imported libraries are available, not just the deepest one
